_comment: Atlas Growth AU :: RECOVERY pass over excluded_officp.csv, mirroring clients/atlas-growth/recover-generic-uk-config.json. The main config deliberately refuses the generic construction buckets — and, Australia-specifically, 'concrete contractor' and 'excavating contractor' — because they are mostly driveways, slabs and earthworks and would flood the list. This pass takes them back ONLY when the business NAME says underpinning / restumping / foundation / levelling work — the pairing qualify-leads.js cannot express as a single rule. Deterministic, $0, no re-scrape. Run: qualify-leads.js --in <run>/excluded_officp.csv --config recover-generic-au-config.json --out <run>/recover, then append recover/leads_clean_qualified.csv to the main qualified list (dedupe on place_id).

qualify_rules._r: 0. RECOVERY SCOPE GATE — recover ONLY rows the main pass dropped at its positive allow (drop_reason 'not_in_icp'). Without it the generic type net below readmits entities the main config removed ON PURPOSE (a drain firm named 'Structural Drainage Solutions' typed 'Drainage service | Contractor' would come straight back). Works because excluded_officp.csv carries the drop_reason column qualify-leads.js appends. CAVEAT: pointed at a file WITHOUT a drop_reason column, qualify-leads.js skips the rule with a WARN on stderr and the pass silently degrades to type+name only — read the WARN line.
qualify_rules.label: not_a_recovery_candidate

qualify_rules._r: 1. The generic type net. These are the buckets the main config's allow deliberately omits. In Australia the ones that matter most are 'concrete contractor' (slab lifting and house levelling firms are routinely primaried this way) and 'excavating contractor' / 'earthworks' (house raising and underpinning). 'building restoration service' is in the MAIN allow, not here. 'waterproofing service' is here, not in the main allow: a basement-waterproofing firm comes back only when its NAME says basement/underpinning, so the wet-area membrane trade stays out. 'pest control service' is here for the same reason: a restumper primaried pest control (termite-damage repair) comes back on an ICP name token; a pure termite firm does not. UPDATED AT THE 2026-09-20 PROBE: 'structural engineer' and 'civil engineer' (substring: also 'Civil engineering company') moved here from the main config's primary deny — Mainmark and Buildfix are typed as engineers; 'drilling contractor' (Surefoot Underpinning Specialist), 'tradesmen' (7 of 149 Brisbane primaries, 3 Melbourne), 'service establishment' (a generic secondary on 46 of 119 Melbourne rows), 'flooring contractor' (Concrete Lifting Services), 'retaining wall supplier', 'masonry contractor', 'bricklayer' added from the probe's type distribution.
qualify_rules.label: not_generic_contractor

qualify_rules._r: 2. The NAME must actually claim the work. This is the precision half of the pair — keep it strict. Australian vocabulary: 'restump', 'reblock', 'relevel', 'house raising', 'slab lift', 'resin inject' are the trade's own words; 'underpin', 'subsidence', 'foundation', 'levelling' are shared with the UK/US. 'structural' is in because 'XYZ Structural Repairs' is how a general builder advertises this line — but 'structural engineer' rows have a different drop_reason (off_icp_primary) and rule 0 refuses them, so the token cannot readmit a practice. Deliberately NOT included: 'concrete' or 'concreting' (every driveway firm), 'building' (matches everything), 'excavation' / 'earthmoving' (lays NEW foundations — adjudicate/PROMPT.md classes that 'no'), 'waterproofing' (bathroom trade). THE BRAND_FAMILIES TERMS ARE INCLUDED — all term strings from atlas-growth-au-config.json's brand_families, copied verbatim and lowercase so the two lists cannot drift (UK GATE 3 / P8 lesson: brand-named rows died on the name gate because a brand name carries no trade vocabulary, contradicting the keep-and-flag directive). Rule 0 still means only a main-pass 'not_in_icp' row can get this far, so a brand term can never rescue something a DENY removed.
qualify_rules.label: name_not_icp

qualify_rules._r: 3. NO REVIEW FLOOR IN THIS PASS — CHANGED AT THE 2026-09-20 MAPS PROBE (measured on 305 probe rows). The UK version repeated the main floor (review_count >= 5) here. In Australia that repetition stranded 49 ICP-NAMED rows: a generic-typed row dies in the main pass as not_in_icp (rule 4 runs before the floor), arrives here, passes the type net and the name gate, and then died on this floor because its review_count was blank or 1-4 — and the unrated / low-rated recoveries could not take it back because their scope gate demands drop_reason 'too_small', which this row never carried. Victims: Restumping Melbourne (blank), OzRestumping (blank), Sunbury Restumping (blank), House Levelling (blank), Underpin Solutions (2), Affordable Underpinning Solutions (4), Titan Reblocking would have survived, Gold Star Reblocking (3), Melbourne Reblocking (3), Heritage Reblocking & Underpinning (2), Brisbane Underpinning and Structural Repairs (2), Underpin Brisbane (1), Raise My House (blank). The name gate above IS the precision here — a row reaches this rule only with a construction-trade type AND an underpinning/restumping/foundation token in its name — so the floor added nothing but loss. Ghost-pin risk accepted and bounded: a no-website, sub-5-review, ICP-named duplicate pin goes to the no-website recovery track (STEP 5d) and dies in the adjudication for lack of site text, at $0. Rule 0 still makes this a not_in_icp-only pass.
qualify_rules.label: unreachable_guard
